name: Major depressive disorder with seasonal pattern
summary: Recurrent major depressive episodes with a regular seasonal onset and remission, usually autumn/winter onset. The only FDA-approved drug indication is prevention of seasonal major depressive episodes with extended-release bupropion (Wellbutrin XL, Aplenzin, and generic XL products). Bright light therapy is a first-line non-drug treatment for acute winter depression (CANMAT 2023, Level 1). No new SAD approvals were found for 2024 to 2026.
plainSummary: Seasonal affective disorder is depression that comes back at the same time each year, most often in fall and winter. Light therapy, talk therapy, and some medicines can treat it or help prevent it.

approved.indication: Prevention of seasonal major depressive episodes in patients with a diagnosis of seasonal affective disorder (SAD).

dosing.start: 150 mg once daily in the morning (Aplenzin 174 mg), started in autumn before symptoms begin
dosing.target: 300 mg once daily (Aplenzin 348 mg) after 7 days
dosing.max: 300 mg/day (Aplenzin 348 mg); higher doses not assessed in SAD trials
dosing.notes: Continue through winter; taper and stop in early spring (reduce 300 mg to 150 mg before stopping). Moderate to severe hepatic impairment: max 150 mg every other day (Aplenzin 174 mg every other day); consider reducing dose in mild hepatic or renal impairment. Swallow whole. Only XL/ER products carry SAD; immediate-release, SR, and Forfivo XL labels do not.

formulations: Bupropion HCl extended-release (XL) tablets 150 mg, 300 mg (Wellbutrin XL and generics)
Bupropion hydrobromide extended-release tablets 174 mg, 348 mg, 522 mg (Aplenzin and generic)
boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: Current or prior bulimia or anorexia nervosa
Abrupt discontinuation of alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, or antiepileptic drugs
MAOIs (concurrently or within 14 days), including linezolid or IV methylene blue
approved.plainSummary: Long-acting bupropion is an antidepressant that can be started in the fall to help prevent winter depression in people who get it every year. It is stopped in the spring.

source.label: DailyMed: Wellbutrin XL (bupropion HCl extended-release) prescribing information

verified.note: Wellbutrin XL (effective 2026-02) and Aplenzin (DailyMed setid 6494d2d9-0ce4-4126-b1c7-49684395942b, effective 2026-03) labels checked for indication, SAD dosing, contraindications, and boxed warning. A scan of DailyMed bupropion labels found SAD on Wellbutrin XL, Aplenzin, generic bupropion HCl XL, and generic bupropion HBr ER, but not on IR, SR, or Forfivo XL. Approval year (June 2006, Wellbutrin XL) comes from news reports. Efficacy rests on 3 prevention trials; the label does not include treatment of an acute seasonal episode.

offLabel.use: Treatment of an acute winter depressive episode
offLabel.notes: In the Can-SAD RCT, fluoxetine 20 mg/day was about as effective as bright light therapy. FDA-approved for MDD in general (the seasonal pattern is an MDD specifier), but has no SAD-specific labeling. Cochrane (2021) rated the evidence for second-generation antidepressants in SAD treatment as low certainty. Antidepressant boxed warning applies.

references.label: Lam et al. The Can-SAD study. Am J Psychiatry 2006, PubMed
Second-generation antidepressants for treatment of SAD. Cochrane 2021, PubMed

offLabel.use: Treatment of an acute winter depressive episode
offLabel.notes: A placebo-controlled outpatient trial (Moscovitch 2004) found sertraline effective in SAD. Labeled for MDD, not SAD-specific. Usual SSRI cautions and boxed warning apply.

references.label: Moscovitch et al. Placebo-controlled study of sertraline in SAD. Psychopharmacology 2004, PubMed

offLabel.agent: Bright light therapy (non-drug, often combined with antidepressants)
offLabel.use: First-line treatment of acute seasonal (winter) depression
offLabel.notes: Not a medication, but listed because CANMAT 2023 recommends it as first-line monotherapy for seasonal depression (Level 1). A typical protocol is 10,000 lux for 30 minutes each morning. Cautions: can trigger hypomania in bipolar disorder; possible eye strain or headache; check eyes in patients with retinal disease or photosensitizing drugs. Cochrane (2019) found limited evidence for light therapy for preventing SAD.

references.label: CANMAT 2023 Update on Clinical Guidelines for MDD in Adults (PMC)
Pjrek et al. Light therapy in SAD: meta-analysis. Psychother Psychosom 2020, PubMed
